source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Five megawatts makes CyrusOne's Florence campus the largest published data center in Kentucky, and it is small by AI training standards.

Kentucky's disclosed data center base is 9.55 MW across three facilities that publish power figures, with five facilities mapped in total. Most mapped sites do not publish specifications, so 9.55 MW is a floor on disclosure rather than a measure of what is built. The gap between three publishing and five mapped is the limit of what these numbers support.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5 MW of IT load is roughly 125 racks. The campus's 143,000 square feet of technical space and its certifications for financial services, healthcare, federal systems, and audit compliance describe a conventional enterprise and cloud facility built for regulated tenants. Nothing in the published specifications indicates a purpose-built AI training campus.

What the data does not cover is whether the site will be retrofitted for higher-density GPU workloads, whether the local grid can supply those draws, or whether the operator or an acquirer intends to expand it. The suitability score of 50 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, and announced expansion is absent from the record. Kentucky is a modest node in the US data center footprint by published capacity, and published capacity is the only part anyone has measured.
